per_depth.common_affordance: The direct reduction of the two-phase conflict-scheduling condition to bipartite graph two-coloring
Recognizing the explicit sum-3 constraint on labels 1 and 2 as ordinary two-coloring/bipartiteness
The polynomial condition is exactly equivalent to requiring different values on the endpoints of every edge, turning the problem into ordinary graph bipartiteness.

The local sum conditions are exactly equivalent to requiring adjacent machines to have opposite modes, so the problem is graph bipartiteness with component orientation chosen for lexicographic minimality.
The binary domain combined with product 2 makes every flagged pair have opposite settings, so the problem is exactly bipartite graph coloring with component orientation.
The spectral constraint is exactly equivalent to requiring every flagged edge to join machines with different values, making the task graph bipartite 2-coloring.

The fixed values x,y ∈ {1,2} together with the displayed star-shaped matrix make largest-eigenvalue = √5 equivalent to x²+y² = 5, hence x and y must differ and the whole problem is graph bipartiteness.
The factor/product arithmetic collapses the problem to proper 2-colorability of the critical-pair graph.
The balance equation is exactly equivalent, for every non-isolated vertex, to requiring adjacent machines to have opposite modes; therefore the task is simply testing and constructing a bipartition.
The equality sum of m OR-values = 3m, together with modes restricted to 1 and 2, forces every pair to have opposite modes, turning the problem into bipartite graph coloring.
